name: Contest Engine
description: A reusable contest engine in which participants submit performances and a host judge scores them on a configurable rubric; the highest total wins, and a tie on the rubric goes to the stronger hidden performance (each contestant's declared skill plus luck, drawn every round). Without a bound judge every submission is scored at the rubric midpoint, so skill and luck decide and the run's diagnostics say the judge was a stand-in.

prompt.default: Present the strongest response to the challenge.

luck.description: Spread of each round's hidden performance around a contestant's skill; 0 = the more skilled always performs better.

participants.description: skill (0 to 1) is private: the hidden quality behind each round's performance.

brief.situation: Participants respond to the same challenge: {$inputs.prompt}
brief.rules: Each participant submits once per round. Submissions are judged blind on the configured rubric. Scores accumulate and the highest total wins; a tie goes to the stronger performance over the contest.

roles.contestant: Create a strong submission using your assigned approach while responding directly to the challenge.

performance.description: Hidden running total of skill plus luck, one draw per submission: breaks rubric ties.

submit.description: Submit your performance for this round.

judge.instructions: Judge the submission on its own merits against the shared prompt.

reasoning.description: Coherent support for its claims or choices.

with.text: A concise response that addresses the challenge with a clear claim, supporting reason, and practical implication.

leaders.description: The two best contestants: highest rubric total, then stronger hidden performance (one sort, so it scales to large fields).

winner.description: The single top scorer (a rubric tie goes to the stronger hidden performance), or null when that ties too.

judged.description: Whether a bound judge scored every submission; false means the rubric scores are the midpoint stand-in and skill and luck alone decided.

winning_score.description: The top rubric total, or null when no judge scored it.

invariants.why: A contest needs at least two contestants: give inputs.participants two or more rows.
